A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Sparse-to-Dense research work. All nine pages of each, including Table 1, Figure 1, equations, and Appendices A-C, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 report original acceptance-rate and wall-time experiments. Appendix C and Figure 1 report hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: The same original benchmark experiments in Table 1 and hyperparameter ablations in Appendix C and Figure 1 are retained.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same text-guided selection of visual KV caches during prefilling, sparse drafting with shared model parameters, and parallel verification using dense attention.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MLVU and the short-, medium-, and long-duration VideoMME subsets. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LayerSkip and Streaming as comparators to STD for both LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct across the same benchmarks.

E3.justification: Both report the same models, chain-of-thought prompting, batch size 8, K plus textual-token count of 1024, and draft length gamma = 9. Acceptance-rate and wall-time metrics and the appendix ablation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Figure 1 retain the same gamma and K sensitivity analyses on MLVU using LLaVA-OneVision-7B, with unchanged curves and accompanying findings.

E5.justification: Section 4 states in both versions that experiments are repeated three times with different random seeds and averages are reported. Neither adds uncertainty intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All Table 1 entries match, including STD's 1.94x speedup on MLVU with Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct. Section 2's token-prediction findings and Figure 1's ablation results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The cache-selection definition, Section 3.3 I/O derivation and acceptance-rate condition, and Appendix A's mathematical definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same claims of training-free, plug-and-play, lossless acceleration without an additional trained draft model, reporting up to 1.94x wall-time speedup.

C2.justification: The interpretations involving attention sparsity, LayerSkip's distributional shift, and verification preventing error propagation are retained. The GPU-memory limitation and proposed future CPU offloading are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same Transformers implementation, NVIDIA A100 80 GB hardware, hyperparameters, and 20-line model-conversion statement. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The references and Appendix B retain the same cited works and positioning relative to visual-token compression, sparse attention, and speculative decoding.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 25 May 2025 to v2 dated 18 May 2026. The title, authors, prose, section order, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Visual comparison confirms the same Table 1 structure and Figure 1 plots, axes, legends, captions, and placement. The page layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The later PDF retains the same scientific content, experimental evidence, technical disclosures, limitations, and organization. The updated arXiv version/date stamp does not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's quality.
